subject: Pilot approval request: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode — customer list + rollout plan
related_account: Hexagon Support Systems; Northstar Fintech; Polaris Analytics; Lumen Legaltech
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Pilot approval request: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode — customer list + rollout plan

Priya / Neha — requesting approval to proceed with a controlled pilot for Dedicated autoscaling bounds (hard min/max) + predictive mode.

Why now:
- We’ve got repeated Dedicated escalations around spend caps + ramp-driven queueing (e.g., SUP-28411, SUP-28437).
- Pilot customers are explicitly tying this to renewal/expansion and/or close.

Pilot scope (controlled):
- Feature-flagged per account + per deployment.
- Canary in us-west first, then expand to us-east if metrics are clean.
- Predictive mode is optional per deployment; reactive scaling remains the fallback.

Proposed pilot customer list (initial 4):
1) Hexagon Support Systems (us-west) — primary need: predictable ramp handling; wants predictive scaling.
2) Northstar Fintech (us-east) — primary need: strict max cap; predictive optional.
3) Polaris Analytics (us-west) — POC; needs min baseline + max cap to hit p95 during ramp.
4) Lumen Legaltech (us-west) — compliance-heavy; cares about auditability of config changes.

Guardrails / risk notes:
- Safety invariants enforced: never exceed max, never drop below min.
- Null/absent forecast must not cause downscale (explicit guard + fallback).
- Anti-oscillation: cooldowns + dampening; minimum step size.
- Region capacity shortage risk if customers set high mins: we will gate min>baseline by manual approval and alert on unmet min.
- Deterministic audit: record requested desired, bounded desired, and reason; log config change actor + time.

Success criteria (pilot exit):
- No regression to Dedicated latency SLO for pilot deployments.
- Bound-hit and queue buildup events are observable + alertable; on-call has runbook.
- Customers confirm bounds semantics match expectations; predictive mode reduces ramp queueing without oscillation.

Schedule:
- 7/8–7/10: us-west canary (1 internal test deployment + 1 pilot customer)
- 7/11–7/18: expand to remaining pilot accounts (up to 4)
- 7/22: readiness review + decision to expand to us-east (Northstar)
- Target GA decision: week of 8/18 (pending readiness and pilot feedback)

Asks:
1) Approve the pilot customer list + rollout plan.
2) Confirm who is final approver for min-bound exceptions during the pilot (to avoid region capacity surprises).

Attachments:
- Dedicated_Autoscaling_Bounds_Pilot_List_v3.xlsx
- Rollout_Checklist_Autoscaling_Bounds_Pilot.md

Thanks,
Lauren
Product Lead, Dedicated
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pilot approval request: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode — customer list + rollout plan

Approved in principle, with two conditions before enabling any external customer:

1) Kill switch + rollback plan confirmed (per-account flag, and ability to disable predictive while keeping bounds).
2) Clear go/no-go checklist for the canary week: which dashboards/alerts we will watch and what thresholds cause rollback.

Also: please keep the pilot very tight on the first week (1–2 customers max) until we see stable behavior.

-Priya

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 11:18 AM PT
Subject: Re: Pilot approval request: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode — customer list + rollout plan

+1 to Priya’s conditions.

On the min-bound / region capacity risk:
- During pilot, any min > current contracted baseline should require explicit infra approval (I can be the approver, but I want a quick template).
- For deployments where min cannot be met due to shortage, we need a customer-visible “degraded/unmet min” state + internal alerting.

Also please clarify: do we allow customers to change bounds freely during pilot, or do changes go through us?

Neha

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 12:26 PM PT
Subject: Re: Pilot approval request: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode — customer list + rollout plan

Adding a few implementation notes so we’re aligned on what “pilot ready” means:

- Feature flags:
  - account_scoped: autoscaling_bounds_enabled
  - deployment_scoped: predictive_autoscaling_enabled
  - both are runtime-evaluated (no redeploy needed) and can be turned off immediately.

- “Null forecast” guard is in (we clamp to reactive desired; we do not allow prediction to drive down).

- Unmet min handling:
  - Autoscaler will keep requesting min, but we surface unmet_min=true and emit an alert if >10m.
  - We’ll document the mitigation: temporarily lower min, or request additional reserved capacity if we can satisfy.

- Config churn:
  - Suggest we rate-limit bound changes during pilot (e.g., no more than 3 changes/day per deployment) to avoid oscillation due to humans.

If product is okay, I’d recommend first external enablement is Hexagon (us-west) only, predictive off for 24h, then predictive on.

Vanessa

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jul 1, 2025 at 2:09 PM PT
Subject: Re: Pilot approval request: Dedicated autoscaling bounds + predictive mode — customer list + rollout plan

Thanks — incorporating the conditions.

Updates / clarifications:

Rollback / kill switch:
- Confirmed per Vanessa: we can disable predictive independently from bounds.
- We will treat “predictive on” as an explicit pilot phase (not default), with a 24h “bounds-only” soak.

Go/no-go checklist (canary week):
- Watch:
  - p95 latency + queue depth for pilot deployment
  - bound_hit_rate (max) and unmet_min (min)
  - scale events rate (oscillation indicator)
  - prediction staleness + prediction error (if predictive enabled)
- Rollback triggers (initial proposal):
  - sustained queue depth increase >15 min vs baseline AND p95 latency > SLO threshold
  - scale up/down thrash: >6 scale events/hour for >2 hours
  - unmet_min true for >10 min (unless previously acknowledged due to known shortage)

Min-bound approvals:
- Agree: any min > contracted baseline requires infra approval during pilot.
- Neha, if you’re ok being approver, I’ll route requests via a short template (deployment id, requested min, expected duration, region).

Customer config changes during pilot:
- Proposed: customers may request changes, but Redwood applies changes during pilot (to control churn). We’ll reevaluate for GA.

Pilot order (tight first week):
- Week of 7/8: Hexagon only (us-west). Bounds-only for 24h, then predictive.
- Week of 7/15: Add Polaris (us-west) bounds-only, and Northstar (us-east) bounds-only if canary clean.
- Lumen stays “bounds-only” until audit log views are confirmed in Console.

If you both approve with these conditions, I’ll have CS align with the customers on the constrained pilot semantics and schedule.

Lauren
